per_proof_checks.mathematical_check: PARTIAL public reconstruction of the full assigned deduction, with strong checked subarguments. The report correctly builds the deterministic strong response, exact weighted lower-left kernel, slow/high cosine split, integration-by-parts constant and near-diagonal weight lower bound. The truncated kernel gives ∫r^(d-3)dr divergence in d=2,3; complexification and block compression are legitimate. Finite-propagation localization and the explicit nonzero covariance mean H=zeta(Gamma*q), positive Q, k>=∫f and C1 time regularity are checked. Its weighted Sobolev-adjoint transposition is correct and explicitly avoids treating chi as E_s-self-adjoint. The HS Bochner covariance contradiction is also explicit. However, it then uses the raw covariance pairing without constructing F_z,w=1_(0,T) zeta v_u G_w in the original noise completion or reconstructing the local-Radon/time-Schur norm bound and smooth interior time approximation. Those original proof steps justify that ell_chi=W(F_z,w) exists for every real s and every fixed Schwartz phase pair on the SAME W; they are not an unassigned all-s driver result. The source supplies them correctly, but the report does not publicly do so. Author-side knowledge is not inserted to count full reconstruction.

The unchanged witness is fully reconstructed. For Gamma=delta0(dx1)dx2, the covariance seminorm is the L2 norm of the x2 marginal. A nonconstant square plateau chi=psi^2 gives g=chi(x1)chi_second_derivative(x2), with zero marginal, while the square mask zeta=chi(x1)chi(x2) produces marginal -chi(x1)^2∫(chi_prime)^2. Thus V(g)=0 but V(zeta g)>0; tensoring with a nonnegative nonzero smooth time test gives finite positive time variance. Homogeneity has d-alpha=1 and the field is not 2D white noise. This shows failure of that physical mask to descend to the original null quotient, not failure to mask tests before a suitable completion.

The public argument chooses a nonzero Schwartz f with Gaussian transform, g=Lambda^-gamma f, and uses the Fourier transform of |g_hat|^2 to show translated pairings tend to zero. A single sufficiently large spacing keeps every nonzero integer multiple correlation at most half the squared norm, so distinct translated images have a fixed positive distance. Inputs stay bounded and the Bessel multiplier commutes with translations. This is whole-space noncompactness for every gamma>0, without a Schatten endpoint claim or loss of the valid compact-cutoff estimates.

The named unassigned temporal equilibrium input applies for a in(0,1), gives f_a in L2, unit potential and positive H_a mass M_a. Tensor controls f_a tensor q_n/sqrt(M_a) have unit original white-noise norm and time-constant mean q_n/sqrt(M_a). Their distant spatial supports make a fixed smooth finite projection kill them exactly; R_n is then chosen to retain them in its plateau. The public F input e=(0,0,1,0), dual velocity Lambda q_n/||q||H1/2 and Bessel pairing give the positive response c_a=||q||2^2/(sqrt(M_a)||q||H1/2), independent of J,n and r. Unit time length gives the stated sup_R lower bound. The witness uses the full F constant-displacement column, not an E-only uniform-radius contradiction; fixed R compactness survives.

Both unchanged scalar facts are reconstructed: D(t)=xt has full C^(2/3) norm2x and U(1)=exp(x); choosing x=1/(16C^2) makes C(2x)^(3/2)=x/sqrt(2)<x. A pure superlinear growth cost cannot cover small drivers. Separately b1=N^(1/r), all other b_j=0 gives average rth power1 but unbounded maximum. The result does not refute a linear-plus-power cost, averaged bad-block estimate or an admissibly slack bound, and it is not an operator-wave estimate.

The report reconstructs the actual concentrating smooth controls: both variable changes cancel epsilon^(a-2)epsilon^2epsilon^-a, giving unit covariance norm. At t=t0+epsilon y the mean equals epsilon^-a/2 times a fixed positive integral; |y-v|<=2 on the chosen supports gives a positive local lower bound. The Lr scaling is epsilon^(1/r-a/2), proving unboundedness only above2/a, including infinity. Away from t0 the kernel is bounded and the mean is O_t(epsilon^(a/2))→0; at r=2/a a positive norm lower bound excludes every strongly convergent subsequence by further a.e. convergence. Endpoint noncompactness is correctly kept distinct from endpoint unboundedness.

The public construction J_n(h)=(1-2||h-e_n||)_+ is continuous. For each fixed h, its nth coordinate tends to zero and ||h-e_n||^2→||h||^2+1>=1, so J_n(h)=0 eventually. Yet the norm-one witness e_n gives score1-1/2=1/2, whereas the limiting score has supremum0 at h=0. This proves pointwise convergence cannot be passed through this Gaussian-action supremum even with bounded witness norms, without asserting a measurable optimizer or a model-specific variational limit.

The public feature calculation reconstructs the full finite-cutoff witness. The heat test g has finite strictly positive covariance norm, and the time r integral for v is1, giving ||v||^2=||g||^2 nu_a((0,L])<infinity. Compact lambda bumps on opposite sides of L make ∫p=0 and the cutoff integral1; the q norm formula follows because ∫phi_prime phi=0. The report incorrectly says the products p^2/lambda and lambda p^2 are bounded away from0 (R2), but lambda itself stays away from0/infinity on the compact support and p is bounded, already giving the correct needed upper integrability. The explicit derivative identity in r and absolute Fubini yield 〈Phi F,q〉=0; density gives q perpendicular to the closed noise image K. The same calculation for v gives 〈v,q〉=||g||^2>0, and the independent auxiliary Gaussian component has conditional variance||(I-P)v||^2>=|〈v,q〉|^2/||q||^2>0. This fixed positive-cutoff/time feature result does not claim an auxiliary component persists in the canonical nonlinear limit.
